discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moire quantum matter)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that interactions dominate over kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realised this with exquisite device control, showing correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (Nature 556, 2018). The twist angle became a new, continuously tunable knob for quantum matter. The work opened moire physics as a field: correlated magnetism, orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and, in moire transition-metal dichalcogenides, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states without magnetic field. Laboratories around the world, including many outside the traditional centres, now use stacked and twisted van der Waals materials as a programmable platform for strongly correlated and topological electrons. Few discoveries in the last decade have so changed how condensed-matter experimentalists work.
